title: ‘Draft Vaibhav Sooryavanshi into India\'s ODI side’: Big endorsement for the 15-year-old swashbuckler
summary: Former India wicketkeeper-batsman Farokh Engineer has urged that 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi be drafted into India\'s ODI side, arguing the youngster\'s aggressive approach and recent form—including an 81 off 49 in Harare—make him an ideal opener alongside Rohit Sharma. Engineer also suggested moving Shubman Gill down to number four to provide a left-right balance in the ODI order.
content:
Farokh Engineer believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is ready to be drafted into India\'s ODI side. After a mixed start in England where Sooryavanshi played three of five T20Is, the teenager produced strong scores in the three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe, including two fifties and a commanding 81 off 49 on a tricky Harare Sports Club pitch.

Engineer wants Sooryavanshi to open the innings alongside Rohit Sharma and has proposed a revised batting order that would move Shubman Gill down the order. "The ideal situation is Shubman Gill and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Gill is a class player. Gill, I think, is the best batsman in the team now. So, Gill should come at four," Engineer told PTI.

He argued a left-right combination at the top would suit India in ODIs. "Gill is not a guy who lifts the ball. So, a left-right combination would be ideal in ODIs. So, if Rohit is playing, and I think he should be playing, let him open with Sooryavanshi."

The coach-turned-commentator also assessed Sooryavanshi\'s limitations: he is not yet fully comfortable against short-pitched bowling, must adapt more quickly to foreign conditions, and needs to refine shot selection and match awareness. Engineer, now 88 and a veteran who played 46 Tests and five ODIs for India between 1961 and 1975, nonetheless believes these are teachable traits.

"This is probably the right time to draft Sooryavanshi into India\'s ODI side. I don\'t know why people distinguish so much between ODI and T20 because for me, a half-volley is a half-volley. He\'s been getting runs, and he\'s got the confidence to open the innings," Engineer said, stressing that the youngster\'s attacking instincts could give India fast starts in the fifty-over format.

Engineer added that aggressive openers can set the platform for big totals: "He\'ll win more matches for you than he loses. When he gives a start like that, the other players can have time to consolidate the innings and put on a big score." He predicted that anything slightly short would likely be dispatched for six and warned against over-coaching the natural game of a prodigious talent.

Drawing a parallel with past greats, Engineer praised Sooryavanshi\'s innate ability and urged patience from selectors and coaches: "He\'s a genius. Nor was Viv Richards. Viv was the best batsman I\'ve ever seen play. But persevere with Sooryavanshi. He\'ll be a tremendous asset for India," Engineer concluded.

content.content:

Former India wicketkeeper batsmanFarokh Engineeris convinced thatVaibhav Sooryavnashiis ready for ODI cricket too. Recently, India played five T20Is in England, and Sooryavanshi got three games there but failed to live up to expectations. However, in the three T20I series against Zimbabwe that concluded on Sunday night, he scored two fifties and in the final game he smashed a very impressive 81 off 49 balls on a tricky Harare Sports Club pitch.

Engineer wants the teenager to open with Rohit Sharma. He also suggests a new position for the captain and current ODI opener Shubman Gill. "The ideal situation is Shubman Gill and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Gill is a class player. Gill, I think, is the best batsman in the team now. So, Gill should come at four," Engineer told PTI.

Also Read: India losing Abhishek Sharma like they lost SKY: Rise of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and his decline might be connected

"Gill is not a guy who lifts the ball. So, a left-right combination would be ideal in ODIs. So, if Rohit is playing, and I think he should be playing, let him open with Sooryavanshi.

"A batsman like Sooryavanshi is much better at opening because he finds bigger gaps in the field. Virat Kohli can come third. Gill can come fourth, and then we've got a solid batting line-up," he added.

Sooryavanshi, in his limited exposure at the international level so far, has shown some weaknesses, like he is not very comfortable against short-pitched bowling. Plus, he has to learn to adapt to foreign conditions really fast besides understanding that he has to settle down first before he unleashes those big shots of his. Shot selection and ‘who to hit or who to respect’ are the other areas he needs to work on. 88-year-old Engineer, who played 46 Tests and five ODIs for India between 1961 and 1975, however, is convinced that Sooryavanshi will be a good fit in the 50-overs format. For him, T20Is and ODIs are pretty much one and the same thing.

"This is probably the right time to draft Sooryavanshi into India's ODI side. I don't know why people distinguish so much between ODI and T20 because for me, a half-volley is a half-volley. He's been getting runs, and he's got the confidence to open the innings.

"He'll win more matches for you than he loses. When he gives a start like that, the other players can have time to consolidate the innings and put on a big score.

"Anything which is slightly short of length, in Sooryavanshi's curve, is going to go for a six. He learned from his mistakes, and he has learned to curb himself. But don't try to over-coach him. He's not from the MCC manual book, which is completely out of date.

"He's a genius. Nor was Viv Richards. Viv was the best batsman I've ever seen play. But persevere with Sooryavanshi. He'll be a tremendous asset for India," Engineer concluded.
